allProductFacts.label: Temperature trends
allProductFacts.value: Below 130 °C: slow, incomplete reaction and low yield. Above 180 °C: larger products. Authors identify 140–170 °C as an optimum range and choose 150 °C. No complete additional run table or numerical particle sizes are supplied.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 / printed p. 18, Results and Discussion

allProductFacts.label: Initial ph
allProductFacts.value: Starting GaCl3 solution above pH 3 leads to Ga(OH)3 precipitation, which the authors state can form Ga2O3 at 150 °C and affect yield/purity. Initial stock pH below 1 is selected.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 / printed p. 18, Results and Discussion

allProductFacts.label: Zinc excess
allProductFacts.value: Authors recommend 10–20% Zn excess relative to their calculated amount. Too little Zn gives incomplete reaction and lower yield; further excess complicates purification. No individual experiment series or denominator derivation is reported.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 / printed p. 18, Results and Discussion

allProductFacts.label: Self regulation
allProductFacts.value: Authors describe Zn dissolution and oxide formation as regulating Zn2+ and reaction pH into 3.5–7.0. This is their interpretation, not a supplied time-resolved pH trace.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 / printed p. 18, Results and Discussion

allProductFacts.label: Net reaction
allProductFacts.value: 4 Zn + 2 GaCl3 + 4 H2O -> ZnGa2O4 + 3 ZnCl2 + 4 H2. Source reaction representation; gas quantities and evolving speciation were not measured in the supplied report.

source_locator.locator: main PDF p. 2 / printed p. 18, Results and Discussion

allProductFacts.label: Reaction steps
allProductFacts.value: Zn + 2 HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2; ZnCl2 + 2 GaCl3 + 4 H2O -> ZnGa2O4 + 8 HCl. These are the two equations used in the authors' self-regulation explanation.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
